A <header> that is a descendant of <main> loses its implicit banner role, so a screen reader has no header landmark to jump to and <main> claims the site chrome as main content. Evidence and the probe output: artifacts/docs/2026-09-06-e2e-first-real-run.md, failure 6. Fixing it also unblocks the getByRole(banner) scoping that switches.spec.ts uses.

tasks.details: From my own run on 2026-09-06 (6 failed, 11 passed): (1) pages/account.ts — getByLabel with exact:true against labels whose accessible name is Email-star, the required marker is a span inside the label; same for Password, First name, Last name. (2) pages/store.ts:31 — selectOption() needs a native select and the sort control is a Radix button role=combobox; click the trigger then the option. This one blocks the whole funnel, so product, cart, checkout and the payment step have never run. (3) locale-redirect.spec.ts — extraHTTPHeaders loses to the Chromium Accept-Language (probed: it sends en-US); use newContext({locale}). (4) locale-redirect.spec.ts cookies — _medusa_locale and _medusa_country are Secure and the container reaches the app over plain http on host.docker.internal, so assert on the Set-Cookie headers of the response instead. switches.spec.ts also asks for a name matching two lowercase letters while the trigger reads EN, and it needs t-header-not-a-landmark first.
